q: Task Scheduler 里 Optimizer 的第一个方法应该返回什么？

只列出当前没有任何依赖的任务
一个所有依赖都排在被依赖任务之前的线性顺序
按任务名字母顺序排列的列表
why: 第一个方法只需给出一个合法的拓扑序，不要求按时长或名字排序。
why_en: The first optimizer method only has to return any valid topological order, not a sort by duration or name.
options_en: The tasks sorted from shortest duration to longest.
Only the tasks that currently have zero dependencies.
A linear order where every dependency comes before the tasks that depend on it.
The tasks sorted alphabetically by name.

why_en: The second optimizer method must return a parallel schedule: the total makespan plus each task's start and end time.
options_en: A single linear order of all tasks sorted by dependency.
A parallel schedule for a fixed worker count: the makespan plus each task's run interval.
The arithmetic average of every task's duration.
The total character length of all task names added together.

q: 最标准的算法该用什么？
q_en: Which standard algorithm fits this dependency-ordering problem?
options: Dijkstra 最短路径算法
KMP 字符串匹配算法
A* 启发式搜索算法
Kahn's algorithm 做拓扑排序
why: 任务图里没有边权和路径代价，只要处理依赖先后关系，Kahn's algorithm 剥离入度为 0 的节点最直接。
why_en: There are no edge weights or path costs here, only dependency order, so Kahn's algorithm — repeatedly removing zero-in-degree tasks — is the direct fit.
whenOtherWins: 如果依赖之间真的带边权、目标是找最短路径代价，Dijkstra 才有用武之地；这里只是先后关系。
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Graph[Dependency graph] --> Zero[zero indegree queue]
  Zero --> Pop[emit ready task]
  Pop --> Dec[lower dependent indegrees]
  Dec --> Zero
options_en: Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm.
The KMP string-matching algorithm.
A* heuristic search.
Kahn's algorithm for topological sort.
tradeoff: 拓扑排序（只看依赖先后）vs 最短路径/字符串匹配/启发式搜索（不同问题类型，靠代价或模式驱动）

rows: 含启发式的最短路径搜索

q: 补全 Kahn 的两个核心结构：

q: Kahn topological sort 的流程包括哪些步骤？（多选）

options_en: Put zero-in-degree tasks into the queue.
Pop a ready task and append it to the order.
Decrement the in-degree of its dependents.

q: 哪段代码正确构建 reverse adjacency？
q_en: Which code correctly builds reverse adjacency?
options: in_degree = {t.name: 0 for t in tasks}

for t in tasks:
    dependents[t.name].append(t.name)
dependents = task.depends_on
why: 边方向是 dep → task；完成 dep 时，要遍历 `dependents[dep]` 才能减少这些任务的 unmet 计数。
why_en: The edge direction is dep to task, so finishing dep means walking dependents[dep] to decrement those tasks' unmet counts.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入本来就是 dep-to-dependent 的邻接表，就不用再反向构建一次。
options_en: For every task, append the task's own name onto dependents[dep] for each dep it depends on.
Initialize in_degree to zero for every task and stop there.
For every task, append the task's own name onto its own dependents entry.
Point dependents directly at task.depends_on without inverting it.
tradeoff: 反转依赖方向建 dependents 表 vs 直接复用 depends_on 原始方向

q: Kahn topological sort 的时间复杂度是什么？
q_en: What is the time complexity of Kahn topological sort?
options: O(V + E)
O(log V)
why: 构建反向图访问每条依赖边一次，主循环每个任务出队一次、每条边再被更新一次，总量是线性的。
why_en: Building the reverse graph touches every edge once, and the main loop visits each task and each edge once more, so the total cost is linear.
scenario: 任务图有 V 个任务、E 条依赖边，你要确认 Kahn 排序在大图上是否还跑得动。
scenario_en: The task graph has V tasks and E dependency edges, and you need to know whether Kahn's sort still scales on a large graph.
options_en: O of V plus E, linear in tasks and edges.
O of V squared times E.
O of two to the V, exponential.
O of log V.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复取出入度为 0 的任务来生成拓扑序的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kahn's algorithm generates a topological order by repeatedly removing zero-in-degree tasks.

q: 拓扑序和并行调度的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between a topological order and a parallel schedule?
options: 两者完全一样，只是叫法和写法习惯不同而已
并行调度过程完全不需要满足任何依赖关系约束
拓扑序只是合法线性序，并行调度还要决定任务何时在哪个 worker 上运行
拓扑序一旦算出来就自动最小化了整个 makespan
why: 一个合法顺序不会告诉你如何利用多个 worker，也不会告诉你多个 ready task 该优先谁。
why_en: A valid order alone does not tell you how to use multiple workers or which ready task to prioritize when several compete.
scenario: Optimizer 的第一个方法给出拓扑序，第二个方法给出多 worker 的并行计划；面试官问两者到底差在哪。
scenario_en: Optimizer's first method returns a topological order, while the second returns a multi-worker parallel plan; the interviewer asks what really differs.
options_en: They are exactly the same thing, just different naming conventions.
A parallel schedule never needs to respect any dependency constraint.
A topological order is just a valid sequence, while a parallel schedule also decides when and on which worker each task runs.
A topological order automatically minimizes the whole makespan once it's computed.
tradeoff: 拓扑序（只保证依赖合法）vs 并行调度（还要分配 worker 和时间区间）

q: Solution 2 的基本做法是什么？
q_en: What is the basic idea of Solution 2?
options: 忽略依赖关系只按 duration 从长到短排序
按 execution_order 逐个任务，交给最早空闲的 worker
每隔一秒重新扫描一次所有任务状态
把每个任务随机分配给某个 worker

why_en: Fixed-order list scheduling consumes a precomputed order and repeatedly pulls the earliest-free worker off a heap.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务优先级必须随运行进展变化，预先固定顺序会错过新解锁的关键任务。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Order[Kahn order] --> Task[next task]
  Workers[min worker heap] --> Free[earliest free worker]

options_en: Ignore dependencies entirely and sort tasks from longest duration to shortest.
Walk the execution order one task at a time and hand each to the earliest-free worker.
Rescan every task's status once every simulated second.
Assign each task to a random worker.
tradeoff: 消耗预先算好的固定顺序 vs 每次事件重新决策（event-driven）

q: 应该用什么结构维护 worker？

用一个只能后进先出、不能随便取的栈

why_en: A min-heap pops the earliest-available worker in O(log W) time and pushes the updated availability back in.
whenOtherWins: worker 数极小时线性扫描也够用，但 heap 写法更通用、结果也更确定。

A min-heap of (available_time, worker_id) pairs.
A stack that only pops in strict last-in-first-out order.
Encode every worker into a segment of an alphabet bitmask.

q: 补全任务 start time 公式：
q_en: Fill in the task start-time formula:
text: 一个任务的开始时间应为 max({{所有依赖完成的最晚时间}}, {{worker 空闲时间}})，event-driven 版还会纳入当前模拟时间。
why: 任务必须等最后一个依赖完成，同时也必须等有 worker 可用。
why_en: A task starts at the maximum of dependency readiness and worker availability.

q: earliest-start helper 如果对依赖完成时间取 min 而不是 max，会发生什么？

options: 任务可能在某个依赖还没完成前就开始
所有任务都会延迟到最后
只影响没有依赖的任务
不会影响正确性
why: 一个任务要等所有 prerequisite 完成，最早开始时间取决于最后完成的那个依赖。
why_en: A task must wait for its last prerequisite, so using the minimum dependency finish time can schedule it too early.
options_en: The task might start before one of its dependencies has actually finished.
Every task would end up delayed to the very end.
It would only affect tasks with no dependencies.
Correctness would be unaffected.

q: 哪段代码正确计算任务运行区间？
q_en: Which code correctly computes a task's run interval?
options: start = 0; end = earliest
start = min(earliest, worker_free); end = task.duration
start = max(earliest, worker_free); end = start + task.duration
start = worker_free - task.duration; end = worker_free
why: 任务必须同时满足依赖完成和 worker 空闲两个条件，取较晚的那个作为开始时间，再加上 duration。
why_en: A task must satisfy both dependency completion and worker availability, so start is the later of the two, and end adds the duration.
whenOtherWins: 在 event-driven 版本里还要把 current_time 也纳入 max，防止任务被安排到模拟时间之前。
codeSample:
worker_free, worker_id = heapq.heappop(workers)
start = max(earliest, worker_free)
end = start + task.duration
timeline[name] = (start, end)
# max(), not min() -- a task waits for BOTH conditions
options_en: Set start to 0 and end to earliest.
Take the minimum of earliest and worker_free as start, and end equals just the duration.
Take the maximum of earliest and worker_free as start, then add the duration to get end.
Set start to worker_free minus the duration and end to worker_free.
tradeoff: 取 max(依赖完成时间, worker 空闲时间) vs 只看其中一个条件

q: fixed-order worker assignment 的调度循环复杂度主要是什么？
q_en: What is the main loop complexity of fixed-order worker assignment?
options: O(2^V)，枚举任务子集
O(W^V)，枚举 worker 分配
O(V log W)，另有 O(V+E) 预处理
O(1)，与任务数无关
why: 每个任务只做一次 heap pop 和 push，worker heap 大小为 W；拓扑排序预处理仍是线性的。
why_en: Each task does exactly one heap pop and push against a worker heap of size W, and the topological-sort setup stays linear.
scenario: 任务数 V 很大、worker 数 W 较小，你想确认 fixed-order 调度循环会不会先成为瓶颈。
scenario_en: V is large and W is small, so you want to check whether the fixed-order assignment loop becomes the bottleneck.
options_en: O of two to the V, enumerating task subsets.
O of W to the V, enumerating worker assignments.
O of V log W, plus O of V plus E setup.
O of 1, independent of the number of tasks.

q: 这条链对并行调度设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this chain imply for parallel scheduling?
options: 只要 worker 数量够多，这条链也能被压缩到更短时间
把链拆给不同 worker 并行执行就能突破这个下界
无论并行度多高，makespan 都不可能低于这条链总时长，调度必须让它连续拿到 worker
这条链和独立任务同等重要，谁先跑不影响最终 makespan
why: 链上任务必须严格串行，1+8+8+8+1=26 秒是任何调度都无法突破的下界，所以关键链必须优先拿到 worker。
why_en: The chain must run strictly in sequence, so its 26-second total is a hard lower bound no schedule can beat, which is why it must get priority for workers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Setup[setup] --> B1[build 1]
  B1 --> B2[build 2]
  B2 --> B3[build 3]
  B3 --> Final[finalize]
  Final --> Bound[critical path lower bound 26]
scenario: critical-path graph 里 setup→build-1→build-2→build-3→finalize 的 duration 分别是 1/8/8/8/1 秒，这五个任务必须严格顺序执行。
scenario_en: In the critical-path graph, setup, build-1, build-2, build-3, and finalize take 1, 8, 8, 8, and 1 seconds and must run in strict order.
options_en: Adding enough workers can compress this chain to finish faster.
Splitting the chain across workers in parallel can beat this lower bound.
No matter how many workers you have, the makespan can never beat this chain's total duration, so the scheduler must keep it running back to back.
This chain is no more important than the independent tasks, so run order doesn't matter.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the longest dependency chain, and it sets the lower bound on the whole schedule.

q: fixed-order scheduler 在 critical-path graph 上为什么得到 38 秒？
q_en: Why does the fixed-order scheduler produce 38 seconds on the critical-path graph?
options: 调度器其实完全没有检查过任何一条依赖关系
调度器把可用 worker 的数量错误地写死成了一个
Kahn 顺序把 scan 排在 setup 前，worker 先被占满，链晚 12 秒启动
调度器把每个任务的 duration 数值错误地重复加了两遍
why: 固定顺序在 t=0 就承诺了 scan 优先，导致真正决定 makespan 的 build chain 等 worker。
why_en: Fixed-order scheduling commits workers to scans first, delaying the critical chain and producing a 38-second makespan.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Ready[t0 ready tasks] --> Scans[workers take scans]
  Scans --> Delay[setup waits]
  Delay --> Late[build chain starts late]
  Late --> M38[makespan 38]
options_en: The scheduler actually never checks any dependency at all.
The scheduler hard-codes the available worker count down to just one.
Kahn's order lists the scans before setup, so workers get taken by scans first and the chain starts 12 seconds late.
The scheduler mistakenly adds every task's duration value in twice.

q: Kahn 输出顺序为什么不能直接当作最优并行调度优先级？

Kahn's algorithm 一次只能处理单独一个任务
why: 拓扑序只保证依赖合法，不保证把 worker 分配给最影响 makespan 的 ready task。
why_en: Kahn's tie-breaking creates a valid order but does not prioritize work that controls the makespan.
options_en: Kahn's algorithm cannot produce a valid order in the first place.
When several tasks are ready at once, Kahn's order is just insertion order or an arbitrary tie-break, with no idea which sits on the critical path.
Kahn's algorithm ignores every dependency relationship outright.
Kahn's algorithm can only ever process a single task at a time.

q: 哪段排序 key 正确？
q_en: Which sort key is correct?
options: ready.sort(key=lambda task: random.random())
ready.sort(key=lambda task: completion_times[task.name])
ready.sort(key=lambda task: task.duration)
ready.sort(key=lambda task: (-critical_length[task.name], task.name))
why: 负号实现降序 critical_length，任务名作为 tie-break 让相同 priority 的输出确定。
why_en: Sorting by negative critical length prioritizes longer remaining chains and task name breaks ties deterministically.
whenOtherWins: 如果调度目标是 deadline 或 SLA，排序 key 应换成反映这些约束的值，而不是 critical_length。
codeSample:
ready.sort(key=lambda task: (-critical_length[task.name], task.name))
# negative critical_length => longest remaining chain sorts first
options_en: Sort by a random number.
Sort by each task's completion time.
Sort by each task's duration.
Sort by negative critical_length first, then by task name as a tie-break.
tradeoff: 按 -critical_length 排序（保关键链）vs 按 duration/completion_times/随机排序
